title: A user who stakes between snapshot generation and the on-chain pause is silently stranded on a paused, defunded, Pauser-deregistered V1 staker
fingerprintAltNote: `fingerprintAltUnprefixed` is the same hash computed with the submodule-relative contract path (no `lib/phoenix-phase-2-staging/` prefix). The CANONICAL fingerprint - the one the ledger keys on - is the lib-prefixed one above. Recorded so a future reconciliation that normalises paths can still match this finding.
description:
A user who stakes between snapshot generation and the on-chain pause is silently stranded on a paused, defunded, Pauser-deregistered V1 staker

Classification basis (verbatim from the severity-classifier): Low under C4: user-facing availability of a staked position is impacted, but assets are not at risk, recovery is complete and owner-controlled, likelihood is low against a 6-address population, and a designated on-chain detection control specific to this failure exists in the story's post-broadcast checklist. Escalating to Medium would require that control to be absent - which is exactly the reopen trigger recorded above.
impact: An end user's staked NFT position and its future emissions become UNAVAILABLE on a retired contract. No value is destroyed and nothing is transferred to a third party: the position remains on V1, the owner retains `setPauser`/`unpause`, `migrate` is re-runnable by design, and V1 can be re-funded or V2 topped up.
attackPath: 1. No attacker. `snapshot-depletion-stakers.js` freezes the user list at block N; forge's local pass freezes it a second time.

2. `NFTStakerDepletion.stake` is UNGATED during `Migrating` (NFTStakerDepletion.sol:550, audit-20 M-05), and V1 is not actually paused until the `st_<label>_pause` transaction lands on-chain - potentially hours into the Ledger session.
3. A user stakes inside that window. Their address is absent from `users`, so `migrate(users)` skips them.

4. The stated backstop `require(old.totalStaked() == 0, "V1 still holds stake after migrate - widen the snapshot and re-run")` at :1394 cannot catch it: like all of Phase 6 it evaluates in the local pass against pre-broadcast state (see M-01).
5. Step 9 then sweeps V1's reward budget down to a ~1% residual, and V1 has already been unregistered from the global `Pauser`, so a later `Pauser.unpause()` will not reach it.
6. The user is left staked on a paused, defunded, unreachable-by-global-unpause contract, with no automatic detection.
recommendation:
Close the window rather than narrow it: split the pause out of the frozen plan. Either (a) pause all three V1 stakers in a separate, short broadcast BEFORE generating the snapshot, so the user list is taken against an already-frozen contract - the snapshot header's 'does NOT need to be taken after a pause' rationale then no longer applies and the list becomes provably final; or (b) add a hard freshness gate: record the snapshot's `blockNumber` in the JSON (it already is) and `require(snapshotBlock >= block.number - N)` in Phase 0 so a stale list cannot be consumed at all. (b) is cheap and also fixes PR-03's late-failure problem. Independently, keep the story's 'Open items carried to review' instruction - re-run `promotion-ready:snapshot` immediately before the session - as an operator gate.

CLASSIFIER ADDENDUM: option (a) is the only one that CLOSES the window; (b) only narrows it. If (b) is chosen, the conditional-Medium reopen trigger above stays armed.
recommendationQuality: strong - two concrete options with the difference between closing and narrowing stated explicitly
justification: Low under C4: user-facing availability of a staked position is impacted, but assets are not at risk, recovery is complete and owner-controlled, likelihood is low against a 6-address population, and a designated on-chain detection control specific to this failure exists in the story's post-broadcast checklist. Escalating to Medium would require that control to be absent - which is exactly the reopen trigger recorded above.

classification.likelihood: low - requires a real user to stake inside the snapshot-to-pause window. The population is 6 stakers across the three contracts (2 / 146 / 13 units). Probability is a direct function of snapshot staleness, and the story's 'Open items carried to review' already instructs re-running the snapshot immediately before the session.
classification.assumptions: A user stakes during the window; the operator does not re-run the snapshot immediately before the session.
classification.externalRequirements: Live user activity concurrent with the multi-hour Ledger session.
classification.recoverability: Full, by owner action - but manual and undetected until someone looks.

pocNote: No standalone PoC. Evidence is the run-22 mainnet-fork PREVIEW execution of `promotion-ready:dry` at block 25659373 (see the script-audit review artifacts).

severityDebate.whyHeldAtLow: This was the closest call in the set - it is the only candidate with a concrete end-user harm narrative, and its designed backstop is vacuous on the very path that matters. It is held at Low for one decisive reason the other near-Medium candidates lack: a DESIGNATED, SUFFICIENT DETECTION CONTROL EXISTS AND IS SPECIFIC TO THIS FAILURE. Story checklist line 1195 requires the operator to confirm on-chain that 'each V1 staker has `totalStaked == 0`' - which is exactly the condition that catches a skipped user, read from the chain rather than from the local pass. Unlike M-01, whose whole subject is the absence of that control, PR-11's failure mode is inside its coverage. Combined with full recoverability, an owner who retains every lever, a 6-address population, and an operator instruction already recorded in the story, the honest classification is Low.
severityDebate.whyNotDownToQA: Because the harm is real user asset UNAVAILABILITY, not a state-handling nicety, and because the guard the authors wrote to prevent it does not function on the broadcast path. That is a genuine Low, not informational.
severityDebate.oneShotWeight: Applied as ORDERING: L-01, the top Low in the set.
severityDebate.conditionalMediumReopenTrigger: RE-CLASSIFY AS MEDIUM if ANY of the following holds at broadcast time: (a) story-072 checklist line 1195 is still unticked when the Ledger session begins - the sole reason this is Low is that a specific, sufficient detection control is designated, and an unticked control is not a control; (b) the snapshot is older than a documented freshness bound at consumption time; (c) the staker population grows materially beyond the 6 addresses observed at block 25659373. This trigger must be carried into the ledger entry verbatim.

conditionalSeverity.armedIf: Remediation option (b) (freshness gate only) is chosen: it NARROWS the window, it does not close it, so this trigger stays armed. Only option (a) (pause before snapshot) closes it.

vacuousGuardNotePreserved: PR-11's stated backstop `require(old.totalStaked() == 0)` at :1394 is itself a member of the ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast family (it evaluates in the local pass). This is a CITATION of PR-09, not an overlap: PR-11 remains a finding even if the guard were made real, because the user would then merely halt the cutover rather than be silently skipped.

remediationOverlapPreserved.note: A Phase 0 `require(snapshotBlock >= block.number - N)` would narrow PR-11's window and satisfy part of PR-03. If the owner implements PR-03's recommendation in full, re-check PR-11 for partial closure - but do not auto-close it: narrowing a window is not closing it, and the ungated NFTStakerDepletion.stake during Migrating (audit-20 M-05) is unchanged.
